```plato

    //==
    // # Edge flip
    //
    // Regularization. Flipping the shared edge of two triangles swaps which
    // diagonal of their quadrilateral is drawn, changing valence without moving a
    // single vertex — so a flip pass rewrites the face table and leaves the
    // position array alone, and the face COUNT is unchanged.
    //
    // A flip is legal only when the edge is interior AND the diagonal it would
    // draw is not already an edge: flipping onto an existing edge would leave two
    // faces sharing the same pair of vertices, which is not a manifold.
    //
    // The conflict rule claims VERTICES, not faces. Claiming faces is the obvious
    // rule and it is wrong: on an octahedron every equatorial edge sees the SAME
    // two poles, so two face-disjoint flips would each draw the pole-to-pole
    // diagonal and the second would land on the edge the first just made. Four
    // vertices per flip, claimed together, rules that out — and being stricter
    // costs nothing, because a rejected flip is simply reconsidered next pass.

    // True when the two vertices are already joined by an undirected edge.
    AreAdjacent(edges: Array<VertexPair>, a: VertexIndex, b: VertexIndex): Boolean
        => edges.Any(pair =>
            (pair.A.Value == a.Value).And(pair.B.Value == b.Value)
                .Or((pair.A.Value == b.Value).And(pair.B.Value == a.Value)));
```
